Commentary.Commentary: That concludes our coverage of this rain-curtailed match. Looking ahead, we have exciting matches scheduled for Sunday, January 19th. Sri Lanka Women Under-19 will face Malaysia Women Under-19 at 2.30 am GMT, followed by the matchup between India Women Under-19 and West Indies Women Under-19 at 6.30 am GMT. We invite you to join us for the early build-up as well. Cheers!

Kayla Reyneke, the skipper of South Africa Women Under-19, says that this win means a lot for them. Adds that everyone played an important role in this match and ends by saying that they will work on their mistakes and carry on with the momentum.

Tash Wakelin, the skipper of New Zealand Women Under-19, says that South Africa Women Under-19 played really well. Adds that they failed to break the opening stand soon and that is what cost them the game. Ends by saying that everyone was excited to play today and they will keep moving forward.
Jemma Botha is the Player of the Match. She says that their bowlers have worked hard and it is always nice to come up with a win. Ends by saying that she feels great to get this award.
Presentations coming up...

Earlier in the game, the rain shortened the game to a 11-over contest. South Africa Women Under-19 scored a total of 91 runs. They began well, with openers showing good form, but the game shifted after Lourens was dismissed for 21. Jemma Botha played aggressively, scoring 32, but her dismissal in the 8th over was crucial and led to a struggle for momentum. New Zealand's bowlers, especially Ayaan Lambat, significantly impacted the innings, taking three vital wickets.

On the other end, the Proteas bowlers took a bit of time to draw the first blood, but when they got the taste of the blood after picking their first wicket in the fifth over, they started picking the scalps on a regular event. Kayla Reyneke and Monalisa Legodi were exceptional with their spell and bagged three and two wickets, respectively, in their account, which helped the side to seal the deal.

An all-round performance from South Africa Women Under-19! New Zealand Women Under-19 batters failed to make things happen like they wanted. Emma McLeod gave a good start from one end but failed to get any support on the other end. She too was dropped twice in the initial overs and she went on to score 34 but departed in the 7th over. Trails of wickets fell and no batter was able to put up a hefty partnership as they ultimately lost the game by 22 runs.
Fuller one, on middle and leg, Ayaan Lambat flicks it to deep square leg for one. South Africa Women Under-19 beat New Zealand Women Under-19 by 22 runs!
